[EVENT] User asked for tips on where to find warblers in the nature reserve.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips on where to find specific warblers, including:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Yellow Warbler: Near slow-moving streams, ponds, and marshes with dense vegetation.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Common Yellowthroat: In wetlands, marshes, and edges of ponds.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Northern Parula: Near slow-moving water with nearby trees or shrubs.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Yellow-rumped Warbler: In coniferous forests, particularly spruce, fir, and pine trees.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Black-and-white Warbler: In deciduous forests, especially oak, maple, and birch trees.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Magnolia Warbler: In mature deciduous forests with dense canopies.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Blackburnian Warbler: In mature deciduous forests, particularly with hemlock, birch, or beech trees.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] - Chestnut-sided Warbler: In deciduous forests with oak, maple, and birch trees.
